nodes.description: TGDS converts UDP-glucose to UDP-4-keto-6-deoxyglucose. This product resembles the reaction intermediate of UXS1 and acts as an "enzyme-rescue metabolite": it lets UXS1 regenerate its bound NAD+ cofactor in a compartment where free NAD+ is scarce. With TGDS deficient, too little of the metabolite is made.

evidence.reference_title: A missing enzyme-rescue metabolite as cause of a rare skeletal dysplasia.
evidence.snippet: We found that the enzyme TGDS produces UDP-4-keto-6-deoxyglucose, a mimic of the reaction intermediate of the enzyme UXS1, which regenerates the essential cofactor NAD+ within the catalytic pocket of UXS1 by completing its catalytic cycle.

nodes.description: The pathognomonic hand finding (Manzke dysostosis): an accessory bone between the second metacarpal and the proximal phalanx, usually bilateral, sometimes unilateral. It is not obligatory: molecularly confirmed patients have been reported without it. A fetus with compound heterozygous TGDS variants also had middle-finger and hallux anomalies.

evidence.snippet: all with the pathognomonic bilateral or unilateral hyperphalangy caused by an accessory bone between the second metacarpal and proximal phalanx known as Manzke dysostosis

nodes.description: UXS1 (UDP-glucuronate decarboxylase, UDP-xylose synthase) loses activity when its NAD+ cofactor is not regenerated. UXS1 makes UDP-xylose, the sugar donor that starts glycosaminoglycan chains on proteoglycan core proteins; that link is the defining reaction of the enzyme rather than a measurement reported in the cited abstract.
